subject: Post-demo: FinWorks integration — batch embeddings / auth / next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Chris Turner <chris.turner@finworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: FinWorks integration — batch embeddings / auth / next steps

Hey Chris — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so we can unblock your integration tests: 

- Goal: wire FinWorks batch embeddings + reranker into your ingestion pipeline (low-latency inference for document search).
- Questions we want to confirm: which auth mode will you use (API key in Vault vs mTLS), expected batch size and average payload size, and whether you need streaming responses for the reranker.

Immediate next steps I promised:
1) Sample SDK snippet for how to set client timeout, chunking and enable structured output for reranker (attached as integration-snippet.txt).
2) Run a quick smoke test on your staging dataset and share any error logs if you hit 5xx or timeouts.
3) If you see errors, include a raw request payload and the request id from the response (we can correlate with our ingress logs).

If you can share the answers to the auth and batch-size questions I can loop in Rishi (infra) to advise on Dedicated config or routing rules. Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up tomorrow?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: integration-snippet.txt (plain text)

From: Chris Turner <chris.turner@finworks.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: QA Team <qa@finworks.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinWorks integration — batch embeddings / auth / next steps

Hey Jordan —

Thanks for the recap. A few quick answers and an issue we hit during our initial staging run:
- Auth: we plan to start with API keys stored in HashiCorp Vault. We may evaluate mTLS later.
- Batch size: we planned 128 items per request (documents are small, ~4-8 KB each).
- Streaming: not required initially for embeddings; reranker we'd prefer streaming if possible.

Problem: when we posted a batch embeddings request from our ingestion job we got intermittent 5xx responses (mostly 502/504). Attached is the top-of-log excerpt (error_log.txt) and a sample request payload (I’ll send batch_payload.json in a follow-up).

Example output from our pipeline:
---
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 102400

Response: 504 Gateway Timeout
Request-Id: 98765-abcde
---

Can you advise where to look? We haven’t changed anything in our client besides increasing batch size for throughput.

Chris
Chris Turner
Head of Platform Integrations, FinWorks
chris.turner@finworks.com

Attachment: error_log.txt (text, 12KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Chris Turner <chris.turner@finworks.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinWorks integration — batch embeddings / auth / next steps

Hi Chris — Dylan from Support/SE here, thanks for the logs — that helps. A couple quick asks to help us repro: 
1) Can you paste the raw JSON body of one of the requests (or attach batch_payload.json) and the exact SDK call you used (language + client version)?
2) Can you set a higher client timeout locally (60s) and retry once to see if the 5xx becomes a 200 or a more informative error?
3) Turn on verbose request logging (we use X-Request-Id to correlate) so we can find the ingress entry.

Two suggestions off the bat:
- If your single-request size is >1MB it can trigger LB timeouts for some routing configs; chunking to ~64-128KB per RPC often avoids that.
- For Dedicated customers we recommend configuring max_concurrent_requests and enabling streaming for rerankers to keep latency predictable. I’ll loop in Rishi to propose concrete Dedicated or Hosted tuning.

Proposed short-term mitigation (try this in staging):
- Set client timeout = 60s
- Reduce batch_size to 32 and re-run one job
- If using our JS/Python SDK, enable streaming=true for reranker calls

Send the payload and we’ll triage against our logs.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Chris Turner <chris.turner@finworks.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: QA Team <qa@finworks.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinWorks integration — batch embeddings / auth / next steps

Dylan — attaching the payload as requested (batch_payload.json). We are calling from our Java ingestion service (redwood-sdk-java v0.9.1). The request that failed looks like this (redacted):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  --data-binary @batch_payload.json

Response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 20:41:22 GMT
Content-Length: 0
Request-Id: 98765-abcde

Notes: individual documents average 6KB, full batch file is ~768KB. We attempted a retry and observed the same 504. We will try the timeout bump and reduced batch size and report back.

Attachment: batch_payload.json (sample, 768KB)

Chris

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Chris Turner <chris.turner@finworks.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinWorks integration — batch embeddings / auth / next steps

Thanks for the payload and logs, Chris — I looked up Request-Id 98765-abcde in our ingress traces. Summary and recommended actions below.

Triage summary:
- Root cause: Large single RPC (~768KB) + short default upstream timeout on the routing path caused a gateway timeout when a backend shard hit temporary CPU pressure. Not an SDK auth issue.
- Evidence: matching Request-Id across ingress + backend logs showing processing spike at the same timestamp.

Short-term mitigations (doable in staging now):
1) Reduce client batch size to 32 items (goal: per-RPC payload ~64-128KB).
2) Increase client-side timeout to 60s. For Java SDK v0.9.1, set client.setRequestTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60)); or use the curl --max-time flag.
3) Retry with exponential backoff (2 retries) for 5xx/504 observed — will reduce transient failure surface.

Recommended platform changes (we can coordinate a Dedicated tuning call):
- If you need large batches, request we create a temporary routing policy that pins your requests to a pool with higher upstream timeouts and larger request body limits. This is a short-lived workaround during bulk ingestion.
- For reranker paths, enable streaming responses (reduces end-to-end latency and memory for large queries).
- If/when on Redwood Dedicated, configure max_concurrent_requests and increase per-route request-body-size.

I’ll create a short runbook and a support ticket to track this (FW-2027-0421). Jordan, can you please propose a 30-min window for us + FinWorks to implement the mitigation and verify?

Appended quick Java snippet (from integration-snippet.txt) — use this to set timeouts and smaller chunks:

// Java SDK (pseudo)
RedwoodClient client = RedwoodClient.builder().apiKey(System.getenv("RW_API_KEY")).build();
client.setRequestTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60));

List<List<Document>> chunks = chunkDocuments(docs, 32);
for (List<Document> c : chunks) {
  client.embeddings().createBatch(c);
}

If you want, we can also run a joint load test against a staging route while you ramp batch size to find the sweet spot.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Infra & Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/FW-2027-0421
